opening.headline: Depending on the nature of the evaluation item, choose the appropriate method among code scoring, model scoring, or human scoring and learn how to increase the reliability of model scoring.
body: Let's say there are four evaluation items. Are the emotional classification labels correct, are the essential phrases included, is the summary to the point, and is the tone polite? If all items are scored the same way, some items will be judged too rigidly and others will be scored unnecessarily expensively.

In this lesson, we compare the speed, reliability, scalability, and flexibility of three grading methods. We will see how the results differ when the same answer is judged by exact match and model scoring, and we will look at ways to increase the reliability of model scoring. Lastly, we provide commentary on examples of directly dividing the rubric for open-ended responses.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the characteristics of code scoring, model scoring, and human scoring
You can select a scoring method appropriate for the nature of the evaluation item.
A rubric creation method can be applied to increase the reliability of model scoring.

screens.title: Each item has a different scoring method.
screens.lead: First, read four reviews of an app. As you read, think about how you would score each item.

visual.alt: Illustration of four assessment cards, each with a question mark asking how to score them.
labels: Is the emotional classification label correct?
Does the summary contain the main points?
What scoring method is appropriate for each item?

paragraphs: There are four things to evaluate about an app that categorizes and summarizes customer inquiries. First, is the emotional classification label correct? Second, did the answer contain the required phrases? Third, does the summary contain the key points? Fourth, is the tone polite?

The four items have different characteristics. You can check if the emotional label is correct by comparing it with the correct answer, and look for the string to check if the required phrase is included. There are items that can be judged by rules like this. On the other hand, it is difficult to determine whether the summary contains the key points and the tone is polite, and must be read and judged.

Having every item read and scored by a human would be accurate, but slow and expensive. Grading everything by rules is fast, but it results in incorrect judgments on items that require judgment. The question we will address in this lesson is which scoring method is appropriate for each item.

callout.label: question of the day
callout.text: How should we divide items that can be judged by rules and those that must be read and judged, and how should each be scored?

screens.outro: First, let's recall how we have evaluated items that are difficult to automatically grade.

screens.title: Items that are difficult to automatically grade
screens.lead: How do you evaluate items that are difficult to automatically grade? When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: Does the way people read each time handle scale?
items.answer: Human grading is the most flexible and high quality, but it is slow and expensive. This may be fine when you have a few dozen evaluation sets, but if you have to reread hundreds of evaluation sets every time you change them, it quickly becomes a bottleneck. So, if possible, we avoid human grading and only use it where necessary.

items.prompt: Can you trust it if you leave the grading to the model?
items.answer: Model scoring is fast and flexible, so it can be used even for complex decisions. However, you should not trust and use it from the beginning. Reliability must first be confirmed and then scale up. Specific ways to increase reliability are covered in the demonstrations in this class.

items.prompt: What criteria should be used to choose a method?
items.answer: The principle of the document is to choose the fastest, most reliable, and most scalable method. If judgment can be made with rules, code scoring comes first, when judgment is needed, model scoring comes first, and if that is not enough, then human scoring comes first.

screens.outro: Let’s compare the characteristics of the three methods one by one.

screens.title: Features of the three scoring methods
screens.lead: Select each tab to compare the features and appropriate uses of code scoring, model scoring, and human scoring.

visual.alt: Bar plot comparing three scoring methods along four axes: speed, reliability, scalability, and flexibility.

tabs.label: Code grading
tabs.body:
This is a method of automatically judging by writing rules in code. The fastest, most reliable and highly scalable. Instead, it is rigid in making subtle judgments that are difficult to establish as rules.

There are two representative rules: An exact match compares the output to the reference answer, such as `output == golden_answer`. Include phrases ensure that key phrases are included in the output, such as `key_phrase in output`. It is suitable for items where the correct answer is clear, such as sorting labels or checking essential phrases.

tabs.label: Model scoring
tabs.body:
This is a method in which the scoring model judges the output according to the rubric. It is fast, flexible, scalable and suitable for complex decisions. Write about items that are difficult to write about as rules, such as whether the summary contains the main points or whether the tone is polite.

However, you need to check its reliability first. The scoring model is scaled up after checking with some samples to see if it matches human judgment. Specific ways to increase reliability will be discussed in the subsequent demonstration.

tabs.label: human grading
tabs.body:
This is a method where people directly read and judge. It is the most flexible and high-quality of the three methods, but it is slow and expensive, so it should be avoided if possible.

But that doesn't mean it's useless. It is used as a standard to calibrate whether the automatic scoring results match human judgment, and human judgment is the starting point when creating a rubric for model scoring. You can understand that it is not used to handle scale, but rather for precise confirmation.

tabs.label: Principles for choosing
tabs.body:
Pick the fastest, most reliable, and most scalable method first. If you put it in order, first check to see if code scoring works, if not, model scoring, and then use human scoring only for the parts that are still lacking.

Even within one evaluation, each item may have different methods. Rather than sticking to just one method, it is common to mix and match them according to the nature of the item.

screens.outro: Now that we've identified the features, let's directly compare how the results differ if the same answer is scored in two ways.

screens.title: Differences in results between exact match and model scoring
screens.lead: Switch between the two states below to compare how the same model answer performs differently in exact match scoring and model scoring. The standard answer is that refunds are possible within 7 days.

visual.alt: A tabular illustration of the baseline answer and two model answers being judged differently in exact match and model scoring.
labels: You can get a refund within a week after purchase

states.label: Exact match scoring
states.body:
Exact match only sees the output as a string identical to the reference answer.

Model answer A is: You can get a refund within a week after purchase. It has the same meaning as the standard answer, but the string is different, so it is judged as a failure. Model answer B is: Refunds are not possible. Since the meaning is opposite and the strings are different, it is also a failure.

I can't tell the difference because both answers are failures. The limitation of exact agreement is that correct and incorrect answers are treated as the same result.

states.label: Model scoring
states.body:
Model scoring compares the meaning of model answers with standard answers.

Model answer A is judged as a pass because the expression within a week means the same as within 7 days. Model answer B is judged as a failure because it runs counter to the criterion that a refund is possible. The two answers will result in different results and the difference in quality will be reflected in the decision.

Therefore, for items with important meaning, code scoring alone is not enough and model scoring is appropriate.

screens.outro: Now that we've established that model scoring is useful, let's look at specific ways to increase its reliability.

screens.title: How to make model scoring more reliable
screens.lead: Select and expand each topic to read five ways to make your model scoring more reliable and why. Try opening the items one by one.

items.title: Write a detailed and clear rubric
items.body: A rubric is a document that describes what the scoring model will look for and judge. Your answer should always mention the company name in the first sentence. Write down the conditions and results clearly, as if they are not mentioned, they will automatically be judged as incorrect. If the criteria are ambiguous, the results will vary each time the same answer is scored.

items.title: Request specific output
items.body: Have the scoring model output either correct or incorrect, or judge it on a scale of 1 to 5. Purely qualitative descriptive assessments are difficult to evaluate quickly and at scale. Narrow down the output format so you can aggregate it right in your code.

items.title: Make an inference first
items.body: Turn on the Think feature in your scoring model to have it infer evidence before making a decision. Evaluation performance improves, especially in tasks that require complex judgment. Rather than jumping to a conclusion right away, it is more accurate to consider the reasons first.

items.title: Leave it to comparison and classification
items.body: LLM is strong at distinguishing between options. Therefore, it is suitable for pair comparison, classification, and grading according to specific criteria to choose which of two answers is better, and avoids evaluating the open creation itself. If the evaluation method is tailored to the model's strength, comparison, the evaluation will be more reliable.

items.title: Corrected by human judgment
items.body: Match model scoring results with human judgment. Some samples are read by humans to check the degree of agreement, and if the degree of agreement is low, the standard is revised. Automated scoring must be consistently aligned with human evaluation to be reliable.

screens.outro: Now that we've confirmed all the methods, let's look at an example of dividing the rubric for free essay answers into an explanation.

screens.title: Case Commentary: Rubric for Free Narrative Responses
screens.lead: The instructor explains the process of completing the rubric for grading open-ended responses by dividing it into code grading and model grading. Select the right arrow to follow the steps.

steps.title: Starting point: A unified rubric
steps.body: The first rubric is one piece. Failure to mention the company name in the first sentence is automatically inaccurate, and your response should be polite and to the point. Since these two conditions are mixed in one sentence, it is impossible to decide how to score it.

steps.title: Step 1: Divide into ruleable part and judgment-requiring part
steps.body: Let’s take the conditions apart one by one. You can find out whether the company name is in the first sentence by looking up the string, so you can judge it with a rule. You must read and judge whether it is polite and to the point.

steps.title: Step 2: Score code for rule-capable parts
steps.body: The inclusion of the company name is scored using a code that checks for the presence of a phrase in the first sentence, such as `key_phrase in output`. It's fast, reliable, and highly scalable. If it doesn't pass this rule, it's immediately judged incorrect and model scoring is skipped.

steps.title: Step 3: The judgment part is a rubric for model scoring
steps.body: Politeness and core inclusion are built into the rubric for model scoring. Be specific about examples and examples of polite tone, and limit your output to either accurate or inaccurate. Turn on thinking so the scoring model first infers evidence and then makes a decision.

steps.title: Step 4: Human reading of the sample to check for agreement
steps.body: Some samples are read and judged by humans and compared to how well they match the model's scores. Human scoring cannot handle the scale, so it is limited to a calibration sample rather than the entire scale.

steps.title: Step 5: If the agreement is low, modify the rubric
steps.body: If agreement is low, read the discrepant cases and find which parts of the rubric were ambiguous. After modifying the criteria to be more specific, check the agreement again with the same sample. This iteration makes model scoring reliable.

screens.outro: Now that we have divided the rubric, let's organize the appropriate methods for the previous four evaluation items in a table.

screens.title: Key points and reflection
screens.lead: Review the key points of this lesson on one screen. Read the paragraph below and proceed to the summary screen.

paragraphs: The scoring method is chosen according to the nature of the item. Code scoring is fast and reliable but rigid, model scoring is flexible but requires validation, and human scoring is precise but slow and expensive.
Model scoring increases reliability through detailed rubrics, specific outputs, inference first, and calibration with human judgment.

checks.q: The standard answer is that a refund is possible within 7 days, and the model responded that a refund can be made within a week of purchase. What is the right decision?

Since the length of the two sentences is different, only human scoring can be used.
Code grading compares meaning and is judged as passing.
Since the meaning is important, the model scoring is appropriate.
checks.explain: Exact match is considered a failure if the strings are different, but the meaning is the same. Items with significant meaning are better judged by model scoring.

wrong.0: If an answer with the same meaning even though the strings are different is considered a failure, it is a misjudgment of quality.
wrong.1: Human scoring is slow and expensive, so avoid it if possible, and model scoring can suffice.
wrong.2: Exact matching in code scoring only compares strings, not meaning.

glossary.def: This is a method of automatically judging by writing rules such as exact match or phrase inclusion in code.
This is a method in which the scoring model judges the output according to the rubric.
This is a method where people directly read and judge.
This is a document that specifically describes the conditions and results to be judged by the scoring model.

misconceptions.fact: Model scoring should first confirm reliability before scaling up. Write down the standard in detail and calibrate it by matching it with human judgment.

misconceptions.myth: Exact match is the most accurate.
misconceptions.fact: An exact match is considered a failure if the strings are different even if the meaning is the same. It is not suitable for items where the meaning is important, and is most reliable only for items where the correct answer is obvious.
Human grading is the most flexible and highest quality, but it is also slow and expensive and should be avoided if possible. It is mainly used to correct automatic scoring.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: The scoring method is chosen according to the nature of the item.
Code grading is fast and reliable, but poor at making nuanced judgments.
Model scoring requires a rubric and reliability check.
Human judgment is used to calibrate automatic scoring.
